answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake funds and build a verifiable service record before taking paid work. Like a wharf that only berths ships carrying a registered manifest, the market checks past jobs, dispute history, and stake size. Forging thousands of identities then demands real capital plus a long river of honest work to earn trust, while a marble-hard slashing rule burns the stake of any identity caught double-selling or colluding. Each fake identity costs the attacker money and time, so flooding the market stops paying.
